en.explanation:
Statement-1 :

Alkali metals dissolve in liquid ammonia to give blue solutions.

✅ True

Explanation: When alkali metals (Li, Na, K, etc.) are dissolved in liquid ammonia, they form deep blue conducting solutions at low concentrations.

Reaction:

The blue color arises from solvated electrons (), which absorb visible light.

Statement-2 :

Alkali metals in liquid ammonia give solvated species of the type .

✅ True

During dissolution, the metal forms metal cations solvated by ammonia molecules, i.e., surrounded by several molecules.

But:

The blue color (Statement-1) is not due to , but due to the solvated electrons ().

Therefore, although both statements are true, Statement-2 does not explain the blue color.
